label: Specification
blurb: Context files, lean context, tests as the spec
why: Tests written by people make agent code correct more often.
Agents follow context-file rules, and every rule adds cost.

label: Looping
blurb: Capped retries, small context, when a green loop isn't done
why: Passing tests don't make an agent's change ready to merge.
Long-running agent loops break work that was already finished.

label: Testing
blurb: Whether test-first still holds, for humans and agents
why: Agents told to work test-first skip the failing test or write tests that can't fail.
Tests from the same source as the code pass wrong code.

label: Security
blurb: Security and other risks, mapped to the OWASP LLM Top 10
why: An agent with private data, untrusted input and a way to send data out gets exploited.
People using AI write less secure code and trust it more.

label: Reviewing
blurb: Why human review stays, and what makes it cheaper
why: Agents produce changes faster than teams can review and release them.
Review time and incidents rise as AI use grows.

label: Delivery
blurb: Small batches, refactoring, staged rollout, and keeping users in view
why: Small batches help, and delivery gets less stable as AI use grows.
AI produces more software, not more value.

label: Measuring
blurb: How to tell whether AI helps, and how far to trust benchmarks, surveys and vendor numbers
why: People feel faster with AI even when timing shows them slower.
Activity numbers like PR counts rise while delivery outcomes fall.

label: Understanding
blurb: Learning, cognitive debt, shared agent context
why: Nobody can be accountable for code they don't understand.
Shared agent memory leaks, goes stale and hides contradictions.

label: Teamwork
blurb: Pairing, mobbing, handoffs, juniors and who carries the review load
why: Juniors ask the model instead of colleagues, so the know-how people pass on by working together thins out.
Review load lands on a few senior engineers as agent PRs multiply.
